:Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 20-11-2022 at about 10.50 a.m., the Petitioner was riding pulsar-200 NS vehicle bearing No.KA-13-EP-1287 on the extreme left side on Gubbi-Tumkur NH-73 road near Mudigere gate, Gubbi Taluk, Tumkur, at that time, the driver of I-20 car bearing No.KA-44-M-5055 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the Pulsar-200 NS.
Due to the impact, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, after the accident, the Petitioner was admitted to Government hospital, Gubbi for first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to Sri Chamarajendra HIMS Teaching hospital, Hassan, wherein he was treated as an inpatient.

He has spent Rs.50,000/- towards medical treatment,
conveyance and the incidental expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as water purifier and was earning Rs.45,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.
4. The Respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of car are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the court through their respective counsel.
But respondent No.2 alone filed objections to the main petition.

Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
It denies the issuance of policy in the name of respondent No.1 in respect of offending vehicle.
Further it contended that the car was not at all involved in the accident.

Further it contended that accident has taken place due to the negligence of the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-13-EP- 1287 and the petition is liable to be dismissed for non joinder of necessary parties.
Further contended that the petitioner was not wearing helmet at the time of accident and was not having valid and effective driving licence.

Further contended that the car was not having the valid and Chethan S. Gowda vs Sachin.L.S on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93498544/
2 effective Fitness certificate as on the date of accident and the insured has willfully handed over the vehicle who was not authorized to drive the vehicle.
On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 20-11-2022 at about 10.50 a.m. on Gubbi-Tumkur NH-73 road, near Mudigere gate,
Gubbi Taluk, Tumkur, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of car bearing No.KA-44-M-5055?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.28 and closed his side evidence.

On the other hand,
Respondent No.2 examined its Officer as RW.1 and closed its side evidence.

8. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2 upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 9. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 20-11-2022 at about 10.50 a.m. due to the rash and negligent driving of the car bearing Regn.No.KA-44-M- 5055 by its driver.
10. On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Regn. No.KA-44-M-5055 by its driver.
11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-28.
He has re-iterated the Petition averments in his chief-affidavit.

Ex.P-1 is the certified copy of charge sheet, Ex.P.2 is the certified copy of order sheet in CC.No.992/2023, Ex.P.3 is the certified copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the certified copy of notice issued u/s 133 of IMV Act, Ex.P.5 is the certified copy of reply to notice, Ex.P.6 is the certified copy Chethan S. Gowda vs Sachin.L.S on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93498544/
3 of wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is the certified copy of IMV report, Ex.P.8 is the certified copy of driving licence of petitioner, Ex.P.9 is the MRI scan report, Ex.P.10 is the Lab report, Ex.P.11 is Ultrasound report, Ex.P.12 is MRI Pelvis for hip joints plain study report, Ex.P.13 and 14 are OPD cards, Ex.P.15 is Medical prescriptions, Ex.P.16 to 19 are OPD bill cum receipt, Ex.P.20 is true copy of complaint,
Ex.P.21 is true copy of FIR, Ex.P.22 is notarised copy of Aadhar card of petitioner, Ex.P.23 to 25 are OPD bill receipts, Ex.P.26 is discharge summary.
Ex.P.27 is inpatient final bill and Ex.P.28 is letter issued by Partha Ceramics.

12. Upon going through Ex.P.20 & 21 FIR and Complaint, they justify the fact that on the complaint lodged before Gubbi Police Station, the concerned Police have registered the case against the driver of car bearing Regn.No.KA-44-M-5055 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
The document Ex.P.1 Charge sheet shows that after thorough investigation, the Gubbi Police have Charge-sheeted the driver of the offending car for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
Ex.P.2 is the order sheet in CC.No.992/2023, shows that the drive of the offending vehicle has pleaded guilty before the court for the offence punishable under section 279, 338 of IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the Spot mahazar which shows it was drawn in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.4 is the notice issued u/s 133 of MV Act.
Ex . P.5
is the reply given to notice.
The document Ex.P.6 is the wound certificate shows that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.7 is the IMV report which shows that accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects and also justify the fact of involvement of vehicle in question in the accident.
13. In the cross examination, nothing has been elicited to show that he was cause for the accident.
He has admitted that the wound certificate shows only laceration wounds.
He has also admitted that he has not undergone any surgery and he was treated conservatively.
14. Further, the Respondent No.2 got examined its officer as RW.1.
In his examination in chief he deposed that the policy issued in the name of Respondent No.1 in respect of offending vehicle was valid at the time of accident.
In the cross examination he has admitted that he is not an eyewitness and deposing on the basis of documents.

He has admitted that charge sheet is filed against respondent No.1.
15.
The learned counsel for Respondent No.2 vehemently argued that due to negligence of the petitioner the accident was taken place.
She further argued that PW.1 in his cross examination at para 2 admitted that "It is true to suggest that the bike has hit the front right bumper of the car".
Therefore the accident was caused by negligence of the petitioner.
16. For correct understanding the evidence should be red its entirety/wholly.
A perusal of the entire evidence of PW.1, it disclose that it is nothing but a stray admission.
The said portion of cross examination would give a sense of which parts of the both vehicles are in contact with each other in the accident.
Which does not mean that he has hit the car.
The charge sheet clearly disclose that due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, said accident was taken place.

Even Ex.P.2 certified copy of the order sheet in CC.992/2023 clearly disclose that the driver of the offending vehicle namely Sachin.L.S. who is respondent No.1 herein has pleaded guilty before Learned Magistrate.

Therefore it is clear that the accident was taken place due to negligence of the Chethan S. Gowda vs Sachin.L.S on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93498544/
4 driver of the offending vehicle.
17.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car and in the said accident, but the Petitioner had sustained only simple injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Partly Affirmative'.
18. Issue No. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending car by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
19. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 26 years.
He has produced aadhar card at Ex.P22 to prove his age.
As per Aadhar card, his year of birth is shown as 1997.
The accident took place on 20.11.2022.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident is taken as 25 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
20. Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working as water purifier and was earning Rs.45,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any document to prove his income.

Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e., Rs.16,000/-p.m. as the accident has been occurred in the year of 2023, for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
21. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
22.
It is to be noted here that according to the petitioner, he has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.6 wound certificate shows that the Petitioner had sustained following injuries.

1. There are two lacerated wound over the top of head (over the parietal bone)side by side measuring 2 x 1 cmx  and 3x1x1/2cms.
2. There is a swelling in the area(Haematoma)
3.There is pain over the front of pelvis.
4.There is a abrasion over the dorsum of left hand.
Wherein the doctor has opined that injuries are simple in nature.
23.
In order to prove the gravity of the injuries, the Petitioner is expected to produce documents.
The petitioner has deposed that he incurred expenditure of Rs.50,000/- for his treatment and other expenses.
In this regard he has produced bill cum receipt at Ex.P.23 to 27 amounting to Rs.6,200/-.

As such, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,200/-towards medical expenses as there is no serious Chethan S. Gowda vs Sachin.L.S on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93498544/
5 dispute with regard to those medical bills.

sentences.text: 24. It is the case of the Petitioner that he has suffered permanent disability.

However, petitioner has not examined any doctor and in the absence of physical disability and considering the nature of injury sustained by the Petitioner and the medical expenses incurred for the treatment.
The Ex.P.26 Discharge Summary discloses that he admitted in the Hospital on 24.11.2022 and discharged on 25.11.2022.
Hence, he was in the hospital for a day and as per the wound certificate the injuries were simple in nature.
Keeping in mind all these factors and the expenses incurred for Food and other charges, this Tribunal is of the opinion that awarding global compensation of Rs.40,000/- would be just and proper.

25. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA-44-M-5055.
There is no dispute of the fact that the respondent No.1 is is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending car in question.
There is no dispute of the fact that the policy in respect of said vehicle was valid and effective as on the date of accident.
Hence, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
26. ISSUE No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.40,000/-along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, entire award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
